<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:basictensor}
For every group $G$ there is a natural central extension
\begin{equation}\label{eq:exterior-extension}
 1\longrightarrow H_2(G;\mathbb{Z})\longrightarrow G\wedge G
 \xrightarrow{\,\bar\kappa_G\,}G'\longrightarrow1.
\end{equation}
If $G$ is perfect, then \eqref{eq:exterior-extension} is the universal
central extension of $G$.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:splitting}
Suppose that $G^{\rm ab}=G/G'$ is finitely generated and has no element of
order $2$.  Then
\[
 G\otimes G\cong \Delta(G)\times(G\wedge G),
 \qquad
 \Delta(G)\cong\Gamma(G^{\rm ab}),
\]
where $\Gamma$ is Whitehead's quadratic functor \cite{BrownLoday1987}.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:fingen}
    If $G$ is a perfect finitely generated group, then $G\otimes G$ is finitely generated.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:embed}
    The group $B_n\wedge B_n$ embeds into $B_n'\times (S_n\ \wedge S_n)$.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
The map
$p:B_n\longrightarrow S_n$ given by
$$\sigma_i\longmapsto s_i=\begin{pmatrix} i & i+1\end{pmatrix}$$
is an epimorphism. 
    Define
    $\iota :B_n\wedge B_n\to B_n'\times (S_n\wedge S_n)$
    by $$\iota=\bar{\kappa}_{B_n}\times (p\wedge p).$$
    Suppose $\iota(z)=1$ for some $z\in (B_n\wedge B_n)\setminus\{ 1\}$. Then $z\in\ker\bar{\kappa}_{B_n}$, and $z\in\ker p\wedge p$. Note that $\ker\bar{\kappa}_{B_n}\cong H_2(B_n,\mathbb{Z})\cong C_2$ by a result of Huebschmann \cite[Theorem 5.1]{Huebschmann2012}. Furthermore, Huebschmann shows that $H_2(B_n,\mathbb{Z})$ is generated by the abelian cycle $[\sigma_1\mid \sigma_3]-[\sigma_3\mid\sigma_1]$. One can infer from here that $\ker\bar{\kappa}_{B_n}=\langle \sigma_1\wedge \sigma_3\rangle$. This implies that $z=\sigma_1\wedge \sigma_3$, and therefore $s_1\wedge s_3=(p\wedge p)(z)=1$. On the other hand, $s_1\wedge s_3$ is a generator of $H_2(S_n,\mathbb{Z})\cong C_2$. This essentially follows by inspecting the proof of Theorem 2.12.3 in \cite{Karpilovsky1987}, see also \cite[Proof of Lemma A.1]{Akita+2024}. This contradiction shows that $\iota$ is an embedding.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
